about.title: A laboratory with a human and professional approach
about.lead: We are a laboratory committed to quality, human care, and timely result delivery. Learn about our history, mission, and team.
history: Our laboratory was founded to offer the community reliable, accessible clinical testing performed responsibly. From the beginning, we understood that behind every sample there is a person waiting for clear and timely answers to take care of their health.
Over time, we have grown by incorporating modern technology and strengthening our professional team, always keeping the same commitment: delivering accurate results with respectful and human care.
Today we continue to evolve, adapting to advances in healthcare while preserving what defines us: trust, ethics, and closeness with our patients.

about.vision: To be a laboratory recognized for the accuracy of our results and the human care we provide, becoming a trusted benchmark of excellence in health care.

faq.title: We answer your most common questions
faq.lead: Find clear answers about preparation, turnaround times, and practical aspects of your lab tests. If you still have questions, you can always contact us in the contact section.

items.question: Can I get tests done without an appointment?
items.answer: Yes, we accept walk-ins during business hours. However, scheduling in advance helps reduce waiting times.

items.question: Do you attend children and older adults?
items.answer: Yes, we have trained staff for sample collection in patients of all ages.

items.question: What documents should I bring?
items.answer: Usually you only need an ID and a medical order if your test requires it.

items.question: Do I need to fast before a test?
items.answer: It depends on the type of analysis. Some tests, such as glucose or lipid profile, require 8 to 12 hours of fasting. We recommend checking specific instructions in advance.

items.question: Is a medical order required?
items.answer: Some tests require medical indication, while others can be done by direct patient request.

items.question: How should I prepare for my test?
items.answer: Instructions vary by study. Our team will provide the required recommendations when scheduling your appointment.

items.question: Can I take several tests on the same day?
items.answer: Yes, in most cases multiple tests can be done in a single visit, as long as preparation instructions are met.

items.question: How long does it take to get results?
items.answer: Most tests are delivered the same day or within 24 hours. Some specialized studies may require more time.

items.question: How can I receive my results?
items.answer: You can receive them at our facilities or, if available, via digital delivery to your registered email.

items.question: Is my result information confidential?
items.answer: Yes, we guarantee protection and confidentiality of all data and results according to security and professional ethics standards.

items.question: Do you accept medical insurance?
items.answer: We work with different insurers. We recommend contacting us directly to confirm coverage and requirements.

items.question: How often should I get routine tests?
items.answer: A general check-up is recommended at least once a year. However, frequency may vary according to age, medical history, and your doctor's recommendations.

items.question: How important is it to get tests even if I feel fine?
items.answer: Many conditions may develop without visible symptoms. Clinical tests help detect changes early and prevent future complications.

items.question: At what age should I start preventive check-ups?
items.answer: Check-ups can start in adolescence, but from age 30 onward closer preventive follow-up is recommended, especially with family history.

items.question: Which tests are part of a basic check-up?
items.answer: They usually include complete blood count, glucose, lipid profile, and general urine test. The doctor may request additional studies based on each case.
